question.worked_solution:
To evaluate ${160}^{2},$ we start by writing it out with a multiplication sign:

$$
{160}^{2}={{160\times 160}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}}
$$

Then, we work out $160\times 160.$

First, we figure out the non-zero part and the block of zeros for both numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned}160 & \,⟶\,160 \\ 160 & \,⟶\,160\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that there are $2$ zeros in total.

Next, we multiply the non-zero parts:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{3}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\,\end{aligned} & \,\, & \begin{aligned}\end{aligned} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we join the above with the block of zeros: 

$$
25600=25,600
$$

Therefore, ${160}^{2}=25,600.$
